rows.query: The driver brought a torn home-pressure diary. Three entries from the past week are around 176/102, but the dates on two lines are incomplete and the clinic obtained only one seated reading today after the driver rushed in from the car park. He says the tablets were restarted recently and asks if the lower reading remembered from last year cancels the diary. The nurse records possible sustained elevation but cannot verify the series or use last year's figure as today's pressure.

At follow-up, the driver says his repeated pressures have improved since antihypertensive treatment, yet the dose was changed three weeks ago and he has briefly felt faint when standing at the depot. The referral does not document a completed period of stable control, whether the dizziness impairs driving, or a specialist review of relevant organ damage. A colleague's comment that he looks well is recorded as hearsay rather than clearance.

During night deliveries the driver sometimes sees a second image beside an oncoming vehicle. Closing either eye removes the doubling, but he was symptom-free during this morning's appointment. A routine chart reading was recorded without noting whether glasses were worn, and no examiner measured the position of the double image relative to straight-ahead vision. The nurse does not treat a normal office conversation as proof that the driving symptom has resolved.

The driver reports missing cyclists entering from one side. An old printout says 138 degrees across both eyes, while a recent automated field result carries a low-reliability warning and does not state whether the central area was clear. Neither paper confirms a stable defect or the full testing protocol. The nurse asks for a reliable binocular field assessment before treating either number as a current commercial-driving result.

A phone image of an audiogram shows some thresholds, although the ear labels and the 3000 Hz row are cut off. It is unclear whether the aids were in place during testing. The nurse cannot calculate an unaided better-ear average from the photograph and requests the signed audiology record.

The driver says an earlier workplace screen had passed him, but that screen did not record the frequencies or better-ear calculation. The assessment needs the commercial threshold and any route involving hearing assistance, with the exact boundary preserved rather than rounded.

limitations: The same small reviewed-anchor corpus is used for every method; this is not full-PDF GraphRAG.
Source labels are engineering expectations and need independent review.
Offline vector results use lexical cosine rather than dense embeddings.
Graph expansion starts from hybrid seeds, so results are not an independent retrieval model.
Expected sources are used only after retrieval for scoring.
Recall measures source discovery, not clinical reasoning or licensing accuracy.
